title: Kensington and Chelsea Emergency Help Points
summary: Offline guide to emergency medical help points, urgent care, and local hazards in the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea.
content:
For life-threatening emergencies, always dial 999 first (or 112). Call 105 for power cuts and 0800 111 999 for gas leaks.

1. 24-Hour Emergency Hospitals
- Chelsea and Westminster Hospital (24/7 A&E): 369 Fulham Road, SW10 9NH. From Earl's Court station: ~15 min walk south along Earl's Court Road and Redcliffe Gardens, or bus 328 or C3. From South Kensington station: ~18 min walk southwest along Old Brompton Road and Fulham Road, or bus 14 or 414.
- St Mary's Hospital (Major Trauma Centre): Praed Street, Paddington, W2 1NY. From Notting Hill Gate: ~20 min walk northeast along Bayswater Road/Spring Street, or bus 27 or 390.
- Charing Cross Hospital (24/7 A&E): Fulham Palace Road, W6 8RF (west of borough).

2. Urgent Treatment Centres
- Chelsea and Westminster Urgent Treatment Centre: 369 Fulham Road, SW10 9NH. Located inside the main hospital entrance alongside A&E.
- St Charles Centre for Health and Wellbeing Urgent Care Centre: Exmoor Street, North Kensington, W10 6DZ. From Ladbroke Grove station: ~10 min walk north along Ladbroke Grove and Barlby Road.

3. Local Environmental Hazards
- River Thames (Tidal Reach): Flood exposure along Chelsea Embankment, Cheyne Walk, and Lots Road during combined high tidal surges and intense rain.
- Basement Dwellings: Extremely high vulnerability to surface-water flash flooding in subterranean flats throughout Notting Hill, South Kensington, and Earl's Court.

4. Essential Supplies
- Major supermarkets and commercial pharmacies on King's Road, Kensington High Street, and Portobello Road/Ladbroke Grove supply emergency drinking water, battery power, and basic medical items.

Note: addresses and opening hours may have changed — confirm on arrival where possible.
